description: EAGLE 8.4+ embeds the open-source ngspice simulator (ngspice 26 in 9.6) in the Schematic Editor: parts are made simulation-ready with ADDMODEL/MAPTOMODEL (SPICE prefix, model and pin order stored as attributes and <spice> mappings), sources are configured with SOURCESETUP/DSOURCESETUP, probes are placed with VPROBE/VPPROBE and the SIM dialog runs Operating Point, DC sweep, AC sweep and Transient analyses, including digital and mixed-mode circuits. Covers the commands, analyses, source types, SPICE attributes and file formats, the ngspice-simulation and ngspice-digital libraries and the shipped example models and schematics.

tools.name: SIM
tools.description: Opens the simulation dialog of the Schematic Editor and runs ngspice on the current schematic. The dialog has four tabs: Configuration (choose the analysis and its parameters, then Simulate), Netlist (view or hand-edit the generated netlist and simulate from it), Simulator Output (raw ngspice text) and Plot (interactive waveform plotter). Every part must be simulation-capable and at least one SPICE ground must be connected; since 9.3 the dialog is non-modal and reports when the schematic changed.
tools.usage: SIM   (command line or the SIM toolbar button in the Schematic Editor)
tools.example: Open examples/projects/examples/ngspice/Analog/rcfilter/rcfilter.sch, type SIM, keep Simulation Type = AC (Dec, 1Hz to 500Meg, 500 points) and click Simulate; the Plot tab opens with the filter response.
tools.notes: EAGLE uses the passive sign convention: loads show positive power and sources negative power. Control statements and scripting inside netlists are not supported. Settings are saved to <schematic>.sch.simcfg. Running SIM needs the interactive editor, which after the June 2026 licensing shutdown stops at the Autodesk sign-in window.

tools.name: SIMOPTOGGLE
tools.description: Switches the display of Operating Point results in the schematic on or off. After an O.P. simulation EAGLE annotates nets and parts with node voltages and currents (layer 100 SimOp); this command hides or shows those labels without rerunning the simulation.
tools.usage: SIMOPTOGGLE
tools.example:
SIM (run an Operating Point analysis on KVL.sch)
SIMOPTOGGLE   # hide the O.P. labels
SIMOPTOGGLE   # show them again
tools.notes: Since 8.7 the O.P. result labels can be moved like text objects. See also 'Operating Point analysis (OP)'.

tools.name: ADDMODEL
tools.description: Converts one part, or the whole schematic when everything is selected first, into simulation-capable parts by adding the required SPICE attributes and pin mappings. EAGLE guesses the device type from the first letter of the part name (R, C, L, X ...), offers to convert GND symbols to SPICE ground, and shows a table of all parts with a DONE column, the assumed Spice Type, value and model; the MAP button per part opens the model-loading and pin-mapping steps. In the Library Editor it stores the SPICE type, model and mapping in the device set so every placed part is simulation-ready.
tools.usage: ADDMODEL name ..   (or select all with GROUP ALL / Ctrl+A, then ADDMODEL; also on the part context menu as Add Model)

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Part name(s) to convert; with a selection active the whole selection is processed.

tools.example:
Open examples/projects/examples/ngspice/Analog/convert/spiceconvert.sch
GROUP ALL
ADDMODEL
# answer Yes to convert GND symbols, then click MAP for every row without a green check
tools.notes: Valid SPICE prefixes: R L C K X S W V I G E F H B T O U D Q J M Z. In the Library Editor the device set prefix is used as the first guess for the SPICE type (since 9.0). spiceconverted.sch in the same folder shows the finished result.

tools.name: MAPTOMODEL
tools.description: Opens the mapping dialog that attaches a SPICE subcircuit (.SUBCKT), a model card (.MODEL) or an intrinsic model to a part and maps each symbol pin to the model's input order. If the part is not yet SPICE-compatible, ADDMODEL runs first in the background. When a gate of a multi-gate device is selected, the mapping covers all gates of the device set.
tools.usage: MAPTOMODEL name ..   (also a context-menu item and toolbar button)

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Part (or gate) to map.

tools.example:
MAPTOMODEL U1
# Load Model: choose LM358D.mdl and where to save it,
# then Map Pins: assign each symbol pin the position of the matching node on the .SUBCKT line
tools.notes: A mapping made in the schematic is stored in the part and overrides the library mapping. The pin order starts at 1 and must match the node order of the .SUBCKT/.MODEL line. See the mapgates example (MapMultiGatePart.sch with LM358D.mdl).

tools.name: REMOVEMODEL
tools.description: Removes SPICE model mappings and SPICE attributes from the selected parts. In a schematic it only works on parts that were mapped in the schematic, not on parts whose mapping comes from the library; in the Library Editor it clears the mappings and attributes of all gates of the device.
tools.usage: REMOVEMODEL name

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Part whose schematic-level SPICE mapping should be removed.

tools.example:
REMOVEMODEL Q1
MAPTOMODEL Q1   # remap Q1 to a different transistor model
tools.notes: The release notes spell it 'REMOVE MODEL'; the 9.6 help lists the command as REMOVEMODEL.

tools.name: SOURCESETUP
tools.description: Analog Source Setup: a dialog for the value of a simulation-compatible independent source (SPICE prefix V or I). It sets the DC value, the AC magnitude used by AC sweeps and a transient function (sine, exponential or pulse); other valid SPICE source values can always be typed directly as the part value. If the part is not yet SPICE-compatible, ADDMODEL is started first.
tools.usage: SOURCESETUP name   (also 'Analog Source Setup' on the part context menu and toolbar)

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Voltage or current source part, e.g. V1 or I1.

tools.example:
SOURCESETUP V1
# DC 0V, AC 1, Transient: Sine, offset 0, amplitude 1, frequency 1kHz
# resulting value: DC 0V AC 1 SIN(0 1 1khz 0 0)
tools.notes: The part VALUE holds the resulting SPICE source string. For PWL or SFFM sources type the value with VALUE. See 'VOLTAGE and CURRENT independent sources (V, I)' and the SIN/PULSE/EXP entries.

tools.name: DSOURCESETUP
tools.description: Digital Source Setup: configures the stimulus of a digital source part for digital or mixed-mode simulation. A table has one time column plus one column per output; each row gives a time (0.010s, 10m, 10ms or 10e-3) and a logic value per output, entered by hand or imported from a .csv file. Values are 0, 1 or U, optionally with a strength suffix s, r, z or u (strong, resistive, hi-impedance, undetermined).
tools.usage: DSOURCESETUP name   (or right-click the part > Digital Source Setup)

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Digital source part (DIGSRC, DIGSRC4, DIGSRC8 from ngspice-digital).

tools.example:
ADD DIGSRC4@ngspice-digital
NET ... (connect all four outputs)
DSOURCESETUP X1
# TIME  OUT1 OUT2 OUT3 OUT4
# 0     0    0    0    0
# 10ms  1    0    1    0
# 15ms  0    1    1    1
tools.notes: Connect every output pin to a net before running it. To turn another part into a digital source, map it to a subcircuit containing the ngspice d_source model; DRIVERD1/DRIVERD4/DRIVERD8.mdl in examples/spice/examples are templates. Added in 9.2.

tools.name: VPROBE
tools.description: Attaches a voltage probe to a net or bus so its node voltage is shown in the simulation results. Without any probes the Plot tab shows all named node voltages and all source currents; once probes exist, only probed signals are plotted.
tools.usage: VPROBE ..   (click nets or buses; also a net context-menu item and toolbar button)
tools.example:
VPROBE (click net OUT)
SIM   # Transient: only V(OUT) is plotted
tools.notes: Probes are drawn in layer 101 SimProbes. After COPY/PASTE, place probes again where needed (9.3.1 fix note).

tools.name: VPPROBE
tools.description: Attaches a voltage phase probe to a net or bus so the phase of that node voltage is available in AC simulation results. Use it together with VPROBE to get magnitude and phase (Bode) curves of a filter or amplifier.
tools.usage: VPPROBE   (click nets or buses; also a net context-menu item and toolbar button)
tools.example:
VPROBE (click net VOUT)
VPPROBE (click net VOUT)
SIM   # AC, Dec, 1Hz to 10Meg: magnitude and phase of VOUT
tools.notes: Only meaningful for AC analyses.

tools.name: EXPORT SPICENETLIST
tools.description: Writes a SPICE-formatted netlist of the loaded schematic without running the simulator; only nets connected to elements are listed. Useful to inspect or reuse the netlist in a standalone ngspice run.
tools.usage: EXPORT SPICENETLIST filename;

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: Output file; the simulator's own copies are <schematic>.sch.net in the schematic folder.

tools.example: EXPORT SPICENETLIST rcfilter.sch.net;
tools.notes: The file actually sent to ngspice is <schematic>.sch.final.net (netlist plus the current simulation configuration). EXPORT also writes NETLIST, NETSCRIPT, PARTLIST, PINLIST, SCRIPT and IMAGE.

tools.name: Operating Point analysis (OP)
tools.description: Computes the DC operating point (node voltages and branch currents at start-up) with no further parameters. Results are shown as text and annotated directly in the schematic; there is no plot. Typical uses are checking bias points, Kirchhoff's laws or that a current mirror copies its reference current.
tools.usage: SIM > Configuration > Simulation Type: Operating Point > Simulate   (.simcfg: "simulation type": "OP")
tools.example: Open ngspice/Analog/KVL/KVL.sch (6 V and 12 V sources, 10k/20k/30k resistors), SIM, Operating Point, Simulate; read the node voltages on the schematic, then SIMOPTOGGLE to hide them.
tools.notes: Shipped OP examples: KVL, curmirror, mapgates, Sources/sources.sch.

tools.name: DC sweep analysis (DC)
tools.description: Sweeps one independent voltage or current source between a start and an end value and plots the DC response, for example a supply ramp from 0 to 3 V or MOSFET transfer curves. The Source drop-down lists only parts mapped as independent sources (SPICE type V or I).
tools.usage: SIM > Simulation Type: DC Sweep; Source = <V or I part>, Start, End, # Points   (.simcfg "dc parameters": dc source, dc start value, dc end value)

parameters.name: Source
parameters.description: Independent source to sweep (e.g. V_VG).

parameters.name: Start / End
parameters.description: Sweep range with units, e.g. 0 and 10V.

tools.example: Open ngspice/Analog/Fet_Characterization/FETCHAR.sch: DC Sweep, Source V_VG, 0 to 10V, 500 points; the plot shows the drain current as the gate voltage turns the MOSFET on.
tools.notes: Advanced 'DC Sim Options' on the right side of the dialog normally stay at their defaults.

tools.name: AC sweep analysis (AC)
tools.description: Small-signal frequency analysis between a start and an end frequency, with DEC (logarithmic, per decade) or LIN (linear) spacing. Sources need an AC magnitude (for example AC 1 in the value) to excite the circuit. Use it for filter cut-off frequencies, amplifier gain and phase.
tools.usage: SIM > Simulation Type: AC Sweep; sweep type DEC | LIN, Start frequency, End frequency, # Points   (.simcfg "ac parameters")

parameters.name: Sweep type
parameters.description: DEC = decade/log scale, LIN = linear scale.

parameters.name: Start / End
parameters.description: Frequency range, e.g. 1Hz to 500Meg; a start of 0 is rejected for DEC.

tools.example: ngspice/Analog/opamp/opamp1.sch: AC, Dec, 1 to 10e6, 500 points; add VPROBE/VPPROBE on the output to see magnitude and phase.
tools.notes: Shipped AC examples: rcfilter (multi-stage RC low pass) and opamp (subcircuit op-amp amplifier and low-pass filter).

tools.name: Transient analysis (TRAN)
tools.description: Time-domain simulation between a start and a stop time, for oscillators, timers, pulse responses or digital logic. TMAX optionally limits the maximum internal time step and can usually stay empty. # Points sets the requested resolution and Max # of Points caps what the plotter draws (200-500 and 1000 are recommended).
tools.usage: SIM > Simulation Type: Transient; START, STOP, TMAX (optional), # Points, Max # of Points   (.simcfg "tran parameters")

parameters.name: START / STOP
parameters.description: Time window, e.g. 1ms and 5ms.

parameters.name: TMAX
parameters.description: Maximum time step (advanced, may be left blank).

tools.example: ngspice/Analog/oscillator/Two_transistor_oscillator.sch: Transient, START 20ms, STOP 20.02ms; C1 has SPICEINITCOND 1V so the 100 MHz BJT oscillator starts.
tools.notes: Negative times are rejected. Digital and mixed-mode examples all use TRAN.

tools.name: Digital and mixed-mode simulation
tools.description: Since 9.2 ngspice's digital (event-driven) primitives can be simulated: logic gates, flip-flops, tri-state buffers and file-driven digital sources from the ngspice-digital library, alone or mixed with analog parts through analog-to-digital (ATODB) and digital-to-analog (DTOAB) bridges. Results appear in a dedicated digital plotting mode. EAGLE checks that analog and digital pins are not mixed on the same net.
tools.usage: Place parts from ngspice-digital, configure DIGSRC* parts with DSOURCESETUP, bridge to analog nets with ATODB/DTOAB, then SIM > Transient
tools.example: Open ngspice/MixedMode/mixed.sch (PULSE sources, ATODB bridges, DFF, AND/OR gates, DTOAB and an OPAMP), SIM, Transient 0 to 30m, Simulate.
tools.notes: Examples: Digital/adder.sch, Digital/processing.sch, MixedMode/gates_and_flops.sch, MixedMode/mixed.sch.

tools.name: ngspice 26 (bundled simulator)
tools.description: EAGLE ships ngspice version 26, an open-source mixed-level/mixed-signal simulator based on Berkeley SPICE3f5, in the ngspice folder of the installation (bin\ngspice.exe plus the ngspice-26 manual PDF and source archive). SIM writes a netlist, runs ngspice in the background and reads its ASCII output.
tools.usage: <EAGLE>\ngspice\bin\ngspice.exe (called by SIM); ngspice's own batch mode: ngspice.exe -b <netlist>
tools.example:
"C:\Program Files\EAGLE 9.6.0\ngspice\bin\ngspice.exe" -b rc.cir
# rc.cir: V1 in 0 DC 1 / R1 in out 1k / R2 out 0 1k / .op / .end
tools.notes: The ngspice manual (ngspice-26-manual.pdf) documents all element, source and model syntax. The bundled ngspice.exe runs a netlist in batch mode without the EAGLE editor and without an Autodesk sign-in (checked on 9.6.0 with a small resistor netlist); run this way it reports that it cannot find its init file, so make sure the XSPICE code models in ngspice\lib\ngspice (analog.cm, digital.cm, ...) are loaded before simulating digital parts. Batch mode is general ngspice usage, not an EAGLE command. LTspice export/import was removed in 9.3.

tools.name: Simulation settings and .simcfg file
tools.description: The Configuration tab settings are loaded from and saved to <schematic>.sch.simcfg, a JSON file next to the schematic. It holds the simulation type (OP, DC, AC, TRAN), temperature, per-analysis parameters and the advanced ngspice options (integration method, tolerances, iteration limits), so a schematic reopens with its last configuration.
tools.usage: <name>.sch.simcfg  (JSON keys: "simulation type", "temperature", "ac parameters", "dc parameters", "tran parameters", "settings")

parameters.name: settings.method
parameters.description: Integration method, TRAP in the shipped examples.

parameters.name: settings.reltol / abstol / vntol / chgtol
parameters.description: Relative, current, voltage and charge tolerances (1e-3, 1e-12, 1e-6, 1e-15 in the examples).

parameters.name: settings.gmin, itl1, itl2, itl4, pivrel, pivtol, trtol, srcsteps, rshunt
parameters.description: Further ngspice convergence options, normally left at their defaults.

parameters.name: settings.numpoints / max limit
parameters.description: # Points and Max # of Points of the dialog (500 and 2000 in the examples).

tools.notes: Since 9.2 all fields are saved, not only those of the selected analysis. The meaning of each option is in the ngspice manual.

tools.name: Simulation output files (.sch.net, .sch.final.net, .sim, .sim.proc.log)
tools.description: Each simulation leaves its files in the schematic folder: <name>.sch.net is the generated netlist, <name>.sch.final.net the same netlist plus the current simulation configuration (the file actually passed to ngspice), <name>.sim the raw simulator output (ASCII since 8.6) and <name>.sim.proc.log the system response when launching the simulator, useful for setup problems. When the simulator does not start at all, the .sim.proc.log file is the first place to look.
tools.usage: Written by SIM next to <name>.sch; EXPORT SPICENETLIST writes a netlist on demand
tools.example: rcfilter.sch  rcfilter.sch.simcfg  rcfilter.sch.net  rcfilter.sch.final.net  rcfilter.sim  rcfilter.sim.proc.log
tools.notes: If a model file is not found, the model is left out of the netlist and the result text reports it.

tools.name: Plot tab (waveform plotter)
tools.description: For AC, DC and TRAN runs the Plot tab opens automatically. Drag a rectangle to zoom and double-click to zoom out; moving the mouse traces all signals and shows their values in the legend. Clicking two points opens a measurement table with the x and y differences of all plotted signals (9.2), the signal menu has Select all/Clear all, and waveforms can be saved to the History to compare runs (8.7).
tools.usage: SIM > Plot tab (after an AC, DC or Transient run)
tools.example: Run an AC analysis with C3 = 1nF, change C3's value to 10pF on its line in the Netlist tab, simulate again and recall the first curve from the plot History to compare the gain.
tools.notes: Without probes all named node voltages and source currents are plotted; with VPROBE/VPPROBE only the probed ones. Digital runs use a separate digital plotting mode.

tools.name: Netlist tab (edit and re-simulate)
tools.description: Shows the netlist EAGLE generated and lets you edit it by hand; clicking Simulate from this tab runs the edited netlist instead of regenerating it from the schematic. EAGLE validates the netlist first and flags invalid lines. This is the quick way to do what-if runs, such as changing one component value, without touching the schematic.
tools.usage: SIM > Netlist tab > edit lines > Simulate
tools.example: In the Netlist tab find the line of capacitor C3, replace its value 1nF with 10pF, click Simulate and compare with the previous waveform in the plot History.
tools.notes: Manual edits are not written back to the schematic. SPICE control statements (.control blocks) are not supported.

tools.name: .PARAM text in the schematic
tools.description: A text object on a schematic sheet that starts with .PARAM defines SPICE parameters for the netlist; part values or subcircuits can then reference them in braces. The shipped examples use it for a resistor value (value {rval} with .PARAM rval=10k), for rise/fall times of digital parts and for the turns ratio of the TRANSFORMER subcircuit.
tools.usage: TEXT '.PARAM name=value' on a sheet (multi-line text allowed); reference as {name} in a part value
tools.example:
TEXT '.PARAM rval=10k' (5 70)
VALUE R1 '{rval}'
tools.notes: In hierarchical designs a .PARAM at the top level can set values inside module sheets (hierarchy example). Subcircuits that need parameters are verified since 9.0.

tools.name: VOLTAGE and CURRENT independent sources (V, I)
tools.description: The VOLTAGE (prefix V) and CURRENT (prefix I) parts of ngspice-simulation are independent sources whose part value is a SPICE source specification: a DC value, an optional AC magnitude and phase for AC sweeps, and optionally a transient function (PULSE, SIN, EXP, PWL, SFFM). The DC-sweep source list only offers parts mapped to these types. A zero-volt V source works as an ammeter; ngspice-simulation has an AMMETER part (prefix VCUR_) for that.
tools.usage: VALUE V1 'DC <v> AC <mag> [<phase>] [PULSE(...)|SIN(...)|EXP(...)|PWL(...)|SFFM(...)]'  or SOURCESETUP V1
tools.example:
VALUE V12 'DC 0V AC 0 SIN(0 1mV 1khz 0 0)'
VALUE I1 'DC 0 AC 1 PULSE(0 1e-3 0 1e-9 1e-9 1e-3 2e-3)'
VALUE V2 5V
tools.notes: Default values are 0V / 0A. Positive current flows from the + node through the source to the - node. The Sources examples (sources.sch, trigsources.sch, conventions.sch) show all source types and sign conventions.

tools.name: SIN (sinusoidal source)
tools.description: Damped sine used for transient runs: offset VO, amplitude VA, frequency FREQ, delay TD and damping factor THETA. SOURCESETUP offers it as the Sine transient function; the time-zero value is used for DC analyses.
tools.usage: SIN(VO VA FREQ [TD [THETA]])

parameters.name: VO / VA
parameters.description: Offset and amplitude (V or A).

parameters.name: FREQ
parameters.description: Frequency in Hz (default 1/TSTOP).

parameters.name: TD / THETA
parameters.description: Delay in s and damping factor in 1/s (default 0).

tools.example: VALUE V1 'DC 0V AC 0 SIN(0 3 1khz 0 0)'   # diode example: 3 V, 1 kHz
tools.notes: Syntax from the bundled ngspice-26 manual, section 4.1.2.

tools.name: PULSE (pulse source)
tools.description: Trapezoidal pulse or clock for transient runs: initial value V1, pulsed value V2, delay TD, rise and fall times TR/TF, pulse width PW and period PER. SOURCESETUP offers it as the Pulse transient function; the digital and mixed-mode examples use it as clock and reset signals.
tools.usage: PULSE(V1 V2 TD TR TF PW PER)

parameters.name: V1 / V2
parameters.description: Initial and pulsed value.

parameters.name: TD / TR / TF
parameters.description: Delay, rise time and fall time (TR/TF default to TSTEP).

parameters.name: PW / PER
parameters.description: Pulse width and period (default TSTOP).

tools.example: VALUE V3 'DC 0V AC 0 PULSE(0 3 0 1n 1n 1m 2m)'   # 3 V, 500 Hz clock
tools.notes: Syntax from the ngspice-26 manual, section 4.1.1.

tools.name: EXP (exponential source)
tools.description: Exponential rise and fall for transient runs: from V1 to V2 starting at TD1 with time constant TAU1, then back towards V1 from TD2 with TAU2. It is the third transient function offered by SOURCESETUP.
tools.usage: EXP(V1 V2 TD1 TAU1 TD2 TAU2)

parameters.name: V1 / V2
parameters.description: Initial and pulsed value.

parameters.name: TD1 / TAU1
parameters.description: Rise delay and rise time constant.

parameters.name: TD2 / TAU2
parameters.description: Fall delay and fall time constant.

tools.example: VALUE V1 'DC 0 AC 0 EXP(0 5 1m 0.2m 3m 0.5m)'
tools.notes: Syntax from the ngspice-26 manual, section 4.1.3.

tools.name: PWL and SFFM sources
tools.description: Piece-wise linear (time/value pairs, optional repeat r= and delay td=) and single-frequency FM waveforms are valid values for the VOLTAGE and CURRENT parts (the library description lists DC, AC, PULSE, SINE, PWL, EXP and SFFM). SOURCESETUP has no dialog page for them, so type the value directly.
tools.usage: PWL(T1 V1 T2 V2 ...) [r=<t>] [td=<t>]   |   SFFM(VO VA FC MDI FS)
tools.example:
VALUE V1 'PWL(0 0 1m 5 2m 5 3m 0)'
VALUE V2 'SFFM(0 1 20k 5 1k)'
tools.notes: Syntax from the ngspice-26 manual, sections 4.1.4 and 4.1.5.

tools.name: Linear controlled sources (VCVS, VCCS, CCVS, CCCS)
tools.description: ngspice-simulation contains the four linear dependent sources: VCVS (prefix E) and VCCS (G) are controlled by the voltage between two control pins, CCVS (H) and CCCS (F) by the current through a voltage source named in the VNAME attribute. The part value is the gain.
tools.usage: E: N+ N- NC+ NC- gain | G: N+ N- NC+ NC- transconductance | H/F: N+ N- VNAME gain  (VNAME attribute = controlling V source)
tools.example:
ADD VCVS@ngspice-simulation E1 ...
VALUE E1 10
ADD CCCS@ngspice-simulation F1 ...
ATTRIBUTE F1 VNAME 'V_V1'
VALUE F1 2
tools.notes: See Analog/Sources/sources.sch for E, F, G and H parts wired as examples. The exact name to put in VNAME is the source name as it appears in the generated netlist (check the Netlist tab).

tools.name: NONLIN_ASRC and FN_* behavioral sources (B)
tools.description: NONLIN_ASRC (prefix B) is ngspice's nonlinear dependent source: its value is an expression v=... or i=... of node voltages, branch currents and functions. The FN_ABS, FN_ACOS, FN_ASIN, FN_ATAN, FN_COS, FN_EXP, FN_LN, FN_LOG, FN_SIN and FN_TAN parts are ready-made subcircuits that output a built-in function of the voltage between their control pins.
tools.usage: NONLIN_ASRC value: v=<expr> | i=<expr>;  FN_<func>: output = func(V(NCP,NCM))
tools.example:
VALUE B1 'v=exp(pi ^ i(E_E1))'   # from sources.sch
# trigsources.sch drives FN_SIN/FN_COS/FN_TAN... from one sine source
tools.notes: Available functions and operators are listed in chapter 5 of the ngspice manual. Model files for the FN_* parts are in examples/spice/examples.

tools.name: Digital stimulus sources (DIGSRC, DIGSRC4, DIGSRC8)
tools.description: The ngspice-digital library provides 1-, 4- and 8-output digital sources that wrap ngspice's d_source model; the waveform comes from a text file with one line per time step (time followed by one value per output). DSOURCESETUP writes this table from the dialog or a .csv import.
tools.usage: ADD DIGSRC|DIGSRC4|DIGSRC8@ngspice-digital; DSOURCESETUP <part>; file lines: <time> <v1> <v2> ... (values 0/1/U with optional s/r/z/u strength)
tools.example:
# driverd4_1.dsource.txt
0 0s 0s 0s 0s
5m 0s 1s 1s 0s
15m 1s 0s 0s 1s
20m 0s 0s 0s 0s
tools.notes: Each source maps to a subcircuit such as DRIVERD81 (.SUBCKT with A_SOURCE [...] D_SOURCE8 and .MODEL D_SOURCE8 D_SOURCE (INPUT_FILE="driverd81.dsource.txt")); see ngspice/Digital and ngspice/MixedMode.

tools.name: AMMETER (current measurement part)
tools.description: AMMETER from ngspice-simulation (name prefix VCUR_) is mapped to a SPICE voltage source with value 0V, the usual SPICE way of measuring a branch current: it is a short circuit, and its current appears among the source currents in the results. Insert it in series with the branch whose current you want to plot.
tools.usage: ADD AMMETER@ngspice-simulation (in series with the branch); value 0V
tools.example:
ADD AMMETER@ngspice-simulation VCUR_1 R0 (20 10)
# split the wire to R1 through VCUR_1, SIM > Transient, plot the VCUR_1 current
tools.notes: Used in switches/vswitch.sch, xformer.sch and Sources/conventions.sch. Current direction follows the + and - pins (positive current flows into +).

tools.name: SPICE mapping in the Library Editor
tools.description: Recommended way to get reusable simulation-ready parts: open the device set in the Library Editor and run ADDMODEL, which shows the same mapping table as in a schematic but with one row per gate. Choose the SPICE type, load a model file if the type needs one and map the symbol pins to the model inputs; EAGLE stores the mapping and the model text in the library, so every part placed from it is ready for SIM.
tools.usage: Library Editor > EDIT <deviceset>.dev > ADDMODEL > Spice Type / Load Model / Map Pins > WRITE
tools.example:
OPEN mylib.lbr
EDIT LM358.dev
ADDMODEL   # SPICE type X (subcircuit), load LM358D.mdl, map the pins of both gates
WRITE
tools.notes: Schematic-level mappings override library mappings; REMOVEMODEL in the Library Editor clears the mapping of all gates.

tools.name: SPICEPREFIX
tools.description: Part/device attribute holding the single-letter SPICE element prefix that tells the netlister which kind of element the part is (R, L, C, X for subcircuits, V/I for sources, D, Q, M ...). ADDMODEL fills it from its guess or from the Spice Type chosen in the table.
tools.usage: ATTRIBUTE <part> SPICEPREFIX '<letter>'  (normally set by ADDMODEL/MAPTOMODEL)
tools.example: ATTRIBUTE Q1 SPICEPREFIX 'Q'
tools.notes: Valid prefixes: R L C K X S W V I G E F H B T O U D Q J M Z. In library XML the prefix is also stored as <pinmapping spiceprefix="...">.

tools.name: SPICEMODEL
tools.description: Attribute naming the SPICE model file to use, without the .mdl extension, or empty for intrinsic devices. For parts mapped in the schematic the model file is searched first in the schematic's folder, then in the user-configurable models directory; parts mapped in a library carry the model text inside the library.
tools.usage: ATTRIBUTE <part> SPICEMODEL '<model file name without .mdl>'
tools.example: ATTRIBUTE Q1 SPICEMODEL '2N2222A'   # uses 2N2222A.mdl next to the schematic
tools.notes: A model that is not found is left out of the netlist and the simulation fails with a note. Show it on the symbol with a >SPICEMODEL text.

tools.name: SPICEINITCOND
tools.description: Attribute with the initial condition of a part: the initial voltage of a capacitor or the initial current of an inductor. Needed, for example, to kick-start oscillators in a transient run.
tools.usage: ATTRIBUTE <part> SPICEINITCOND '<value>'
tools.example: ATTRIBUTE C1 SPICEINITCOND '1V'   # Two_transistor_oscillator.sch
tools.notes: Only affects analyses that use initial conditions (transient).

tools.name: SPICEEXTRA
tools.description: Optional attribute whose text is appended to the netlist line after the model name, typically instance parameters such as geometry (L=10 W=20), multiplicity (m=1.0) or an initial switch state (OFF). It passes instance parameters that the mapping dialog does not cover, without editing the model file.
tools.usage: ATTRIBUTE <part> SPICEEXTRA '<extra netlist text>'
tools.example:
ATTRIBUTE M1 SPICEEXTRA 'L=10u W=20u'
ATTRIBUTE S1 SPICEEXTRA 'OFF'
tools.notes: The V_SWITCH part ships with SPICEEXTRA = OFF; several examples use m=1.0.

tools.name: SPICEGROUND
tools.description: A symbol with an attribute SPICEGROUND (empty value) is treated as SPICE node 0. Every simulated schematic needs at least one such ground connected to the circuit; ADDMODEL offers to convert existing GND supply symbols, and ngspice-simulation has a GND device for it.
tools.usage: ADD GND@ngspice-simulation  (or ATTRIBUTE on a ground device: SPICEGROUND '')
tools.example:
ADD GND@ngspice-simulation (0 0)
NET (0 0) (0 5.08)
tools.notes: Missing ground is the most common reason a simulation does not calculate.

tools.name: _EXTERNAL_
tools.description: Attribute (empty value) that marks a device as external: it may have pins but no package and is kept out of the board. All ngspice-simulation and ngspice-digital devices carry it, so sources, probes and ground symbols exist only in the schematic.
tools.usage: ATTRIBUTE _EXTERNAL_ ''   (in the Library Editor device, not in the schematic)
tools.example:
EDIT VOLTAGE.dev
ATTRIBUTE _EXTERNAL_ ''
tools.notes: Must be defined in the library; as soon as a package is assigned the device is no longer external.

tools.name: <spice> pin mapping in library and design XML
tools.description: Simulation mappings are stored in the XML of libraries (inside <deviceset>) and of schematics (inside <part> for schematic-level mappings). A <spice> element contains <pinmapping spiceprefix="..."> with one <pinmap gate pin pinorder> per pin and an optional <model name="..."> holding the full model or subcircuit text, so mapped parts carry their model with them.
tools.usage: <spice><pinmapping spiceprefix="X"><pinmap gate="G$1" pin="P" pinorder="1"/>...</pinmapping><model name="OPAMP">.SUBCKT ...</model></spice>
tools.example:
<spice>
<pinmapping spiceprefix="D">
<pinmap gate="G$1" pin="A" pinorder="1"/>
<pinmap gate="G$1" pin="C" pinorder="2"/>
</pinmapping>
<model name="DMOD">.MODEL DMOD D</model>
</spice>
tools.notes: Defined in doc/eagle.dtd (attributes isusermap and iddevicewide on <pinmapping>). Probes are stored as <probe> elements in net segments.

tools.name: SPICE model files (.mdl) and models directory
tools.description: Model cards and subcircuits live in plain-text .mdl files. MAPTOMODEL loads them and can store a copy; for schematic mappings the file must sit next to the schematic or in the models directory set in Options/Directories (8.7). The Control Panel has a Models branch that lists the available models.
tools.usage: <name>.mdl containing .MODEL or .SUBCKT ... .ENDS; Options > Directories > Models
tools.example:
* 2N2222A.mdl (ships next to Two_transistor_oscillator.sch)
.model 2N2222A NPN(IS=1E-14 VAF=100 BF=200 IKF=0.3 ...)
# referenced by the part attribute SPICEMODEL = 2N2222A
tools.notes: Search order: library-stored model, then the schematic folder, then the models directory.

tools.name: Simulation filter criteria (IsSimReady, RequiresSpiceModel, HasSpiceModel)
tools.description: The Design Manager's Filters tab has criteria for simulation readiness: IsSimReady finds parts with a complete SPICE mapping, RequiresSpiceModel parts whose type needs a model file, and HasSpiceModel parts using a given model. Value criteria accept the same engineering multipliers and units as SPICE (p, n, u, m, k, Meg, G, T; V, A, F, Hz, H, s).
tools.usage: Design Manager > Filters: (IsSimReady), !(IsSimReady), (RequiresSpiceModel), (HasSpiceModel <name>)
tools.example: ((ObjectType = Part) AND !(IsSimReady))   -> selects the parts that still need ADDMODEL/MAPTOMODEL
tools.notes: Filters were added in 9.5 and work in schematic and board; criteria are combined with AND/OR and negated with !.

tools.name: ngspice-simulation.lbr
tools.description: Managed library of 31 simulation-ready schematic-only parts: R, C, L, DIODE, LED, BJT_NPN, BJT_PNP, FET_N, FET_P, OPAMP (5-pin macro model), TRANSFORMER (needs .PARAM RATIO), V_SWITCH, VOLTAGE, CURRENT, AMMETER, the controlled sources VCVS/VCCS/CCVS/CCCS, NONLIN_ASRC, the FN_* function blocks and the simulation GND. Every device is already mapped and carries its model where needed.
tools.usage: ADD <device>@ngspice-simulation   (e.g. ADD R@ngspice-simulation)
tools.example:
ADD VOLTAGE@ngspice-simulation V1 R0 (0 0)
ADD R@ngspice-simulation R1 R0 (10 0)
ADD GND@ngspice-simulation (0 -10)
VALUE R1 1k
tools.notes: Shipped as cache\lbr\ngspice-simulation.lbr and imported into the managed-library cache. Parts have no packages (_EXTERNAL_), so they do not appear on a board.

tools.name: ngspice-digital.lbr
tools.description: Managed library (9.2+) of 23 digital parts for digital and mixed-mode simulation: AND/3AND/4AND, NAND/3NAND/4NAND/5NAND, OR, NOR/3NOR/4NOR, XOR, INVERTER, BUFFER, TRISTATE, DFF, JKFF, the file-driven sources DIGSRC/DIGSRC4/DIGSRC8 and the bridges ATODB, DTOAB and DTOAB_8BIT. Each device contains an ngspice XSPICE digital model (for example d_nor with 1 ns delays).
tools.usage: ADD <device>@ngspice-digital
tools.example:
ADD JKFF@ngspice-digital
ADD ATODB@ngspice-digital   # analog-to-digital bridge for a PULSE clock
tools.notes: Analog and digital pins must not share a net; use ATODB/DTOAB bridges.

tools.name: examples/spice/examples analog model files
tools.description: Example SPICE model files shipped in <EAGLE>\examples\spice\examples for analog parts: OPAMP, QNPN, QPNP, NFET, PFET, DMOD (diode), POT, XFORMER (parameterized transformer), VSMOD (voltage-controlled switch) and the behavioral function models FN_ABS, FN_ACOS, FN_ASIN, FN_ATAN, FN_COS, FN_EXP, FN_LN, FN_LOG, FN_SIN and FN_TAN. They are templates for MAPTOMODEL and the models used by ngspice-simulation.
tools.usage: MAPTOMODEL <part> > Load Model > <EAGLE>\examples\spice\examples\<name>.mdl
tools.example: MAPTOMODEL Q2   # load QNPN.mdl, map C/B/E to model pins 1/2/3
tools.notes: The folder DESCRIPTION calls them the basic example SPICE models shipped with EAGLE 9.6.0.

tools.name: examples/spice/examples digital model files
tools.description: Digital model files in the same folder: AND2, AND3, NAND2, NOR2, OR2, XOR2, INV, TRIS, DFF, JKFF, the bridges ATODB, DTOAB and DTOAB_8BIT, and the digital source templates DRIVERD1, DRIVERD4 and DRIVERD8 that wrap ngspice's d_source model. Use them to make your own library parts simulate digitally.
tools.usage: MAPTOMODEL <part> > Load Model > DRIVERD8.mdl (or AND2.mdl, DFF.mdl ...)
tools.example: Copy DRIVERD4.mdl, change the INPUT_FILE name to mystim.txt, map a 4-output connector part to it and fill mystim.txt with DSOURCESETUP-style rows.
tools.notes: DRIVERD* can be extended to any number of outputs (see DSOURCESETUP help).

tools.name: ngspice example: convert (spiceconvert.sch / spiceconverted.sch)
tools.description: Shows how to turn an ordinary schematic into a simulation-ready one: spiceconvert.sch uses normal library parts, and after selecting all parts and choosing Add Model from the context menu every part is mapped; spiceconverted.sch is the finished result, preconfigured for a transient run (1 ms to 4 ms). Use it to rehearse the ADDMODEL workflow before converting your own schematics.
tools.usage: <EAGLE>\examples\projects\examples\ngspice\Analog\convert\
tools.example: Open spiceconvert.sch, Ctrl+A, right-click > Add Model, map each row, then SIM > Transient; compare with spiceconverted.sch.
tools.notes: Shipped examples open read-only; save a copy to your project folder first.

tools.name: ngspice examples: operating point (KVL, curmirror, mapgates)
tools.description: Three analog examples preconfigured for Operating Point analysis: KVL.sch verifies the expected currents of a two-source resistor network, curmirror.sch checks that both transistors of a current mirror carry the same current, and mapgates/MapMultiGatePart.sch shows how a multi-gate part (LM358D) is mapped to one subcircuit model. Open one and click Simulate to see the annotated operating point without changing any settings.
tools.usage: <EAGLE>\examples\projects\examples\ngspice\Analog\{KVL,curmirror,mapgates}\
tools.example: Open curmirror.sch, SIM > Simulate (OP is preselected), compare the collector currents annotated on the schematic.
tools.notes: mapgates ships LM358D.mdl next to the schematic, illustrating the model search order.

tools.name: ngspice examples: AC and DC sweep (rcfilter, opamp, Fet_Characterization, conventions)
tools.description: rcfilter.sch shows the cut-off frequencies of a multi-stage RC low pass (AC, 1 Hz to 500 MHz); opamp/opamp1.sch uses subcircuit op-amp models (macroopamp.mdl) for a voltage amplifier and a low-pass filter (AC). Fet_Characterization/FETCHAR.sch sweeps V_VG from 0 to 10 V to draw MOSFET turn-on curves (DC), and Sources/conventions.sch demonstrates source sign conventions with a DC sweep.
tools.usage: <EAGLE>\examples\projects\examples\ngspice\Analog\{rcfilter,opamp,Fet_Characterization,Sources}\
tools.example: Open FETCHAR.sch, SIM (DC sweep of V_VG preconfigured), Simulate; change the source to the drain supply to sweep V_DS instead.
tools.notes: Each schematic has a matching .sch.simcfg with the settings.

tools.name: ngspice examples: transient (diode, oscillator, switches, xformer, hierarchy, trigsources)
tools.description: Transient examples: diode.sch (sine-driven LED circuit that demonstrates .PARAM statements), oscillator/Two_transistor_oscillator.sch (100 MHz BJT oscillator with an initial condition on C1 and 2N2222A.mdl), switches/vswitch.sch (voltage-controlled switch with an AMMETER), xformer.sch (parameterized transformer subcircuit, RATIO via .PARAM), hierarchy/h_sim.sch (module-based design with a top-level .PARAM and ZC830A.mdl) and Sources/trigsources.sch (FN_* function sources). Each folder contains the schematic, its .sch.simcfg and any model files it needs.
tools.usage: <EAGLE>\examples\projects\examples\ngspice\Analog\{diode,oscillator,switches,xformer,hierarchy,Sources}\
tools.example: Open xformer.sch, change the .PARAM RATIO text, SIM > Transient 1ms-5ms, Simulate and watch the secondary voltage scale.
tools.notes: Sources/sources.sch (OP) collects every source type: VOLTAGE, CURRENT, E, F, G, H and B sources.

tools.name: ngspice examples: digital and mixed-mode (adder, processing, gates_and_flops, mixed)
tools.description: Digital/adder.sch builds an adder from XOR/AND/OR/BUFFER parts driven by DIGSRC and DIGSRC8 stimulus files; Digital/processing.sch combines JK flip-flops and gates with an analog PULSE source through an ATODB bridge. MixedMode/gates_and_flops.sch drives gates and flip-flops from analog sources and an 8-bit stimulus file (with a .PARAM for rise/fall delay), and MixedMode/mixed.sch mixes resistors, a capacitor and an op-amp with DFF, AND/OR and DTOAB/ATODB bridges. All are transient runs.
tools.usage: <EAGLE>\examples\projects\examples\ngspice\{Digital,MixedMode}\
tools.example: Open MixedMode/gates_and_flops.sch, SIM > Transient 0 to 40m, Simulate; the plot switches to digital mode for logic signals.
tools.notes: The folders contain the DRIVERD*.mdl subcircuits, their *.dsource.txt stimulus files and input.csv (a CSV importable with DSOURCESETUP).
